text: Then Moses answered, "But what if they do not believe me or listen to my voice? They will say, 'The LORD did not appear to you.'"
The LORD said to him, "What is that in your hand?" "A staff," he answered.
"Throw it on the ground," he said. Moses threw it on the ground, and it became a snake, and Moses fled from it.

versions.text: "Throw it on the ground," he said. Moses threw it on the ground, and it became a snake, and he ran from it.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew names Moses again and uses the stronger verb "fled"; restating the name also clarifies the subject after two clauses about the staff and the snake.

text: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Reach out your hand and take it by the tail." So he reached out and caught it, and it turned back into a staff in his hand—
"This is so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has appeared to you."

versions.text: "so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you."
versions.explanation: As printed, verse 4 ends with narration and an em dash, and verse 5 opens a fresh quotation with a lowercase subordinate clause. For oral reading and for verse-by-verse clarity, the sentence should stand on its own; the internal dashes also keep the long list of divine names from stalling the rhythm.

text: The LORD said to him further, "Put your hand inside your cloak." So he put his hand inside his cloak, and when he drew it out, his hand was leprous, white as snow.
"Put your hand back inside your cloak," he said. So he put his hand back inside his cloak, and when he drew it out, it was restored like the rest of his flesh.
"If they will not believe you or heed the first sign, they may believe the second.

But if they will not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, then take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. The water you take from the Nile will become blood on the ground."
But Moses said to the LORD, "Please, Lord, I have never been a man of words—not yesterday, not the day before, not since you began speaking to your servant. I am slow of speech and slow of tongue."
The LORD said to him, "Who gave man his mouth? Who makes him mute or deaf, seeing or blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
Now go; I will be with your mouth and teach you what to say."
But he said, "Please, Lord, send someone else."

Then the LORD's anger burned against Moses, and he said, "What about your brother Aaron the Levite? I know he can speak well. He is already on his way to meet you, and when he sees you his heart will be glad.
You are to speak to him and put the words in his mouth; I will be with your mouth and with his, and I will teach you both what to do.
He will speak to the people for you; he will be your mouth, and you will be as God to him.
And take this staff in your hand, for with it you shall perform the signs."
Then Moses went back to Jethro his father-in-law and said to him, "Let me return to my relatives in Egypt to see whether they are still alive." Jethro said to Moses, "Go in peace."
The LORD said to Moses in Midian, "Go back to Egypt, for all the men who wanted to kill you are dead."
So Moses took his wife and his sons, set them on a donkey, and started back to the land of Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.
The LORD said to Moses, "When you return to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders I have put in your power. But I will harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.
Then say to Pharaoh: This is what the LORD says: Israel is my firstborn son,
and I told you, 'Let my son go, so that he may serve me.' But you refused to let him go; therefore I will kill your firstborn son."
On the way, at a place where they stopped for the night, the LORD met him and sought to put him to death.
But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son's foreskin, and touched it to his feet, saying, "Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me."

versions.text: But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son's foreskin, and touched Moses' feet with it, saying, "Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew simply says "his feet," leaving the referent open; naming Moses adds interpretation not present in the text. If the identification is retained, a footnote noting that the Hebrew reads "his feet" would be helpful.

text: So he let him alone. It was then that she said, "A bridegroom of blood," because of the circumcision.

versions.text: So he let him alone. It was then she said "bridegroom of blood," because of the circumcision.
versions.explanation: The clause needs "that" after "then" and a comma before the quotation; as it stands the sentence stumbles when read aloud.

text: The LORD said to Aaron, "Go into the wilderness to meet Moses." So he went, and he met him at the mountain of God and kissed him.
Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and all the signs he had commanded him to perform.
Then Moses and Aaron went and gathered all the elders of the Israelites.
Aaron spoke all the words the LORD had said to Moses, and he performed the signs before the eyes of the people.
And the people believed. When they heard that the LORD had taken notice of the Israelites and had seen their misery, they bowed down and worshiped.
